conventions.convention: An immersion requires differential injectivity on the entire tangent star, including vectors from different incident simplices. An embedding additionally is a homeomorphism onto its image. Corner adaptation requires face compatibility and a differential fan homeomorphism onto the appropriate tangent orthant or specified face sector.

Strong approximation bounds both values and differential errors on all tangent-star vectors. Shape control means a positive lower bound for barycentre-to-boundary radius divided by diameter on positive-dimensional simplices; it is not claimed for arbitrary iterated barycentric subdivisions.

Fitting identifies overlap subcomplexes by a simplexwise affine isomorphism. A full subcomplex contains every simplex whose vertices belong to it; a nonfull fit is made full by compatible barycentric subdivision before gluing.

A projection-preserving diagram satisfies πF = hr. Each domain simplex maps affinely under r into a simplex of the original D, without requiring vertices to map to vertices. Fitting keeps h and the original r unchanged as point maps.

Admissible boundary data must agree on corner-face intersections and have a differential fan homeomorphic to the union of boundary faces of the tangent orthant. Their pointwise parametrization is preserved, with compatible subdivisions permitted.

Protected-region fitting requires the new pieces and required support stars to lie in an open support neighbourhood whose closure avoids the protected region. Previously fitted pieces outside the support retain their identifications.

The relative bundle theorem requires genuine finite face-compatible product trivializations and a supplied projection-preserving diagram on a closed neighbourhood of the protected subpolyhedron. Boundary triangulation alone, or proper smoothness alone, does not supply these hypotheses.
Both existence theorems declare ambient AC, while their proofs identify only finite choices and say that no essential AC use occurs.

load_bearing.statement: Whole-star smooth embeddings of finite complexes into a smooth manifold without boundary admit arbitrarily small strong C¹ approximations on finite subdivisions fitting in a full subcomplex, with whole-star embedded union. For supplied bundle diagrams with smooth product trivializations, the same fitting keeps h and the original r maps unchanged. Protected-region and corner versions require the stated support separation and adapted face/tangent hypotheses.

For a whole-star smooth immersion f of a finite complex, some δ > 0 makes every strong piecewise C¹ δ-approximation on any finite subdivision a whole-star immersion. If f is an embedding, δ can also ensure embedding. No mesh or shape bound is required.

A piecewise smooth map on a finite geometric complex has face-compatible subdivisions with mesh tending to zero and one positive thickness bound whose secants converge strongly in piecewise C¹. Approximation can fix a neighbourhood of a subcomplex, equal secants outside a prescribed open neighbourhood, and preserve affine target-plane constraints. A sufficiently small approximation on any subdivision of a finite subcomplex extends with prescribed small strong error, unchanged outside its closed star and preserving a vanishing affine-linear correction component; this extension asserts no shape bound.

For a finite whole-star embedding into an orthant whose coordinate zero sets on original simplices are unions of faces, with nonnegative coordinate differentials vanishing precisely on the corresponding zero-set tangent cones, sufficiently small strong approximations preserving those coordinate planes remain embeddings into the same orthant with exactly the same coordinate zero sets.

Under the declared ambient AC hypothesis, a compact Hausdorff second countable smooth manifold with corners with the stated face-preserving smooth atlas has a finite corner-adapted whole-star smooth triangulation. Admissible supplied total-boundary triangulations extend pointwise, allowing compatible subdivisions; the protected closed-neighbourhood version also holds. Corner faces are locally subpolyhedra, and any specified finite union of closed faces is a subpolyhedron.

Assume AC. A smooth bundle with compact total space, compact smooth base and fibre permitting corners, and supplied finite face-compatible product trivializations admits a finite corner-adapted whole-star triangulation F with πF = hr over a supplied finite corner-adapted whole-star base triangulation h:D→B. The map r is affine simplexwise into the original D. The construction is relative to a supplied closed-neighbourhood diagram with a protected subpolyhedron in its relative interior, provided remaining fitting supports avoid it.

published_dependencies.used_for: Underlying simplicial-complex conventions used by the subcomplex supplier.
Subcomplex, closure and star terminology in the assigned definition.
Positive minima for singular values, separation angles, coordinate functions and distances on nonempty compact sets.
Segment integration and derivative-to-value estimates, applied piecewise along subdivided segments.
Compactness of finite Euclidean simplices, unit-direction sets and closed bounded products.
Compact closed separation sets in the embedding-stability argument.
Converting continuous injections on finite compact realizations into homeomorphisms onto their images.
Compatible triangulations of lattice cells, hyperplane-cut fitting cells, corner boxes and product cells.
Face-chain description ensuring that a subdivided overlap subcomplex is full.
Derivative bounds for tapered corrections, chart changes and bundle shifts.
Compactness and Hausdorffness of finite fitting domains and glued realizations.
Finite chart margins allowing sufficiently fine support stars to remain in chart domains.
Declared ambient choice hypothesis in the two existence theorems.
Clipped box self-map arguments proving that small face-preserving perturbations retain smaller cores.
Local collar flows and uniqueness used to identify forward and reverse orbit segments.
Smooth dependence of collar flows on starting points and time, including local extensions across corner coordinate planes.

seams_checked.note: The citing item lem-compact-semialgebraic-families-admit-compatible-finite-triangulations states the manifold supplier faithfully in F3 and the bundle/fitting suppliers faithfully in F4. Steps 8–11 check genuine corner cores and face-compatible bundle charts; steps 19–21 supply positive-width projection-preserving collar diagrams and protected buffers before applying the relative suppliers. The supplier page does not claim triangulation of arbitrary algebraic maps, and the consumer explicitly excludes that strengthening. The shift-and-fitting argument was additionally compared with [Putz, §§1.9–1.10 and 3.3–4.4](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/3C2209F15E20312654B3B2602314144D/S0008414X0005450Xa.pdf/div-class-title-triangulation-of-fibre-bundles-div.pdf).
